item.title: Fushimi Sake District: Kyoto's Historic Brewing Quarter — Guide
item.description: Fushimi, in the south of Kyoto, is one of the three greatest sake-brewing centres in Japan, rivalled only by Nada in Kobe. Its fame rests on its water: the soft, mineral-rich springs here give a sake traditionally regarded as gentler and rounder than most. Dozens of breweries, some four centuries old, cluster along willow-lined canals of black-timbered storehouses, and several open their doors for tastings and tours. The Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum tells the story with old tools and a tasting, and in spring pleasure boats drift along the canal past the storehouses — an atmospheric and grown-up counterpoint to the temples.

item.title: Saijo Sake District: Brick Chimneys and Brewery Streets — Guide
item.description: Saijo, in Higashihiroshima, is one of the three most important sake-brewing towns in Japan, alongside Nada in Kobe and Fushimi in Kyoto. What makes it exceptional for visitors is its compactness: within a few minutes' walk of the station stand around half a dozen historic breweries, their white plastered walls, black-tiled roofs and tall red-brick chimneys forming an unmistakable townscape. Most open their doors to visitors with free or inexpensive tastings, wells of the soft local water you can drink from, and shops selling their own labels.

item.title: Akita Sake: One of Japan's Finest Sake Regions — Guide
item.description: Akita is one of Japan’s most celebrated sake prefectures — pure snowmelt water, high-quality Akita rice and cold winters that allow slow fermentation produce sake of exceptional clarity and elegance. Over 40 breweries welcome visitors, and some offer toji (master brewer) experience days where you join actual brewing. The Yamamoto, Kariho and Dewatsuru labels are internationally known. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Akita City, Yuzawa & beyond Hours Brewery/bar hours Admission Tastings vary; experiences ~¥5,000 Time needed 1–2 hours (or full brewing day) Best time Year-round; brewing winter What to Try Clean, elegant Akita sake from 40+ breweries.

item.title: Morioka Craft Beer: Iwate's Brewery Scene — Guide
item.description: Morioka’s thriving craft beer scene is anchored by breweries like Iwate Kura Beer and a cluster of tap rooms near the Kitakami River, showcasing local ingredients including Nanbu wheat and Iwate-grown hops. Tasting flights pair naturally with the city’s famous three-noodle district, making a brewery crawl a perfect complement to a Morioka food tour. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Morioka, Iwate Hours Tap room/pub hours (evenings) Admission Pints & flights vary Time needed 1–2 hours Best time Year-round; weekend brewpub events What to Try Local brews from Iwate Kura Beer and others.
